title: Type Policies & Field Policies
description: Control cache behavior with type policies and field policies in Apollo Client.

data.text: Type policies let you define how a specific GraphQL type is read from and written to the cache. The most important property is `keyFields`, which tells Apollo which field(s) uniquely identify an object. By default, Apollo uses `id` or `_id`.

data.title: Type policy example
data.content: Custom type policy with keyFields and field modifiers.

data.text: Field policies control how individual fields are cached and merged. You can use `read` functions to transform cached data, `merge` functions to combine paginated results, and `keyArgs` to control cache key generation.

items: read: Transform or compute field values from cache.
merge: Combine incoming data with existing cache data.
keyArgs: Specify which arguments affect cache uniqueness.
data.title: Field Policy Options

data.text: When using `merge` for pagination, always include a `keyArgs` strategy or Apollo may merge unrelated queries together. Use `false` for keyArgs if the field should never be split by arguments.
data.title: Pagination Merge
Type & Field Policies Key Points
points: Type policies define cache behavior per GraphQL type.
keyFields specifies the unique identifier for a type.
data.takeaway: Type and field policies give you fine-grained control over Apollo Client caching behavior.
